Singapore East (Katong/Joo Chiat, Geylang, Bedok, Tampines, Changi)
Singapore West & North (Jurong, Bukit Timah, Holland V, Ang Mo Kio, Bishan, Woodlands)
Vietnam (Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi, Hoi An)

cuisines.n: Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee)

P.ad: 135 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The modernist 1960s presidential palace where NVA Tank 843 crashed the gate on 30 April 1975, ending the war. Frozen-in-time state rooms, war-command bunker and telecoms basement. National monument; daily ~07:00-18:00, 80,000d.

P.ad: 01 Cong xa Paris, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The twin-spired red-brick French cathedral (1863-1880) built with imported Marseille materials, on the square opposite the Post Office. UNDER RESTORATION since 2017 (interior closed to visitors; completion pushed to ~2027, scaffolding coming off by early 2026) — view the exterior.

P.ad: 125 Cong xa Paris (Hai Ba Trung), Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Working 1886-1891 post office (architect Alfred Foulhoux; often mis-credited to Eiffel) with a vaulted iron-truss hall, painted maps and a portrait of Ho Chi Minh. Ranked among the world's most beautiful post offices; still operational.

P.ad: 73 Mai Thi Luu, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Saigon's most atmospheric Taoist temple, built by the Cantonese community in 1909, thick with incense smoke and carved wooden deities incl. the Hall of Ten Hells and a turtle pond. Obama visited in 2016. Free, ~07:00-18:00.

P.n: Nguyen Hue Walking Street & People's Committee Building
P.ad: Nguyen Hue Boulevard, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The city's 900 m pedestrian boulevard (a former canal, walkerised 2015) running from the floodlit French Hotel de Ville / People's Committee Building (1898-1909, viewed from outside) and Ho Chi Minh statue down to the Saigon River. Liveliest at night.

P.ad: 07 Cong Truong Lam Son, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Flamboyant 1897-1900 French Beaux-Arts theatre, once seat of South Vietnam's Lower House, now a national relic staging the acclaimed bamboo-circus A O Show and The Mist.

P.ad: 36 Ho Tung Mau, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The 262 m lotus-bud tower (2010) with a helipad wing and the 49th-floor Saigon Skydeck, the city's first observation deck, giving 360-degree views over the river. Open daily ~09:30-21:30.

P.n: Ho Chi Minh City Museum (Gia Long Palace)
P.ad: 65 Ly Tu Trong, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: City-history museum in an 1885-1890 neoclassical palace that served the French governor, President Diem (as Gia Long Palace) and the RVN Supreme Court, with a wartime bunker/tunnel beneath. Traces Saigon from prehistory to reunification.

P.ad: 2 Nguyen Binh Khiem, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Vietnam's national-history collection in a 1926-1929 Indochinese-style building beside the Botanical Gardens: Cham and Oc Eo antiquities, Dong Son drums, a mummified noblewoman, plus water-puppet shows. Closed Mondays.

P.n: Fine Arts Museum (Bao tang My thuat)
P.ad: 97A Pho Duc Chinh, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The city's leading art museum in a yellow 1929-1934 Franco-Chinese mansion of the wealthy Hua family, with the first lift in Saigon; holds lacquer, silk and war-era painting plus Champa/Oc Eo relics. Closed Mondays.

P.ad: 42 Nguyen Hue, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A crumbling 1960s nine-storey block (once housing for US advisers) reborn as a vertical warren of independent cafes, boutiques and bars, each balcony overlooking the walking street. Slow lift ~3,000d, or take the stairs.

P.n: Book Street (Duong Sach Nguyen Van Binh)
P.ad: Nguyen Van Binh, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A shaded 144 m pedestrian lane beside the cathedral and Post Office lined with 20-plus publisher stalls, secondhand-book stands and book cafes, plus author events. Free; best in the evening.

P.ad: Bui Vien Street, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Saigon's neon backpacker strip in the Pham Ngu Lao quarter (on the map since Lonely Planet's 1993 guide) — bar stools spilling into the road, street food and live music. Pedestrianised nightly; peaks Fri-Sun.

P.n: Ho Chi Minh Museum - Dragon House Wharf (Nha Rong)
P.ad: 1 Nguyen Tat Thanh, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The 1862-1863 twin-dragon-roofed former Messageries Maritimes house on the riverfront from which the 21-year-old future Ho Chi Minh sailed to France in June 1911; a branch of the Ho Chi Minh Museum since 1979. Closed Mondays.

P.ad: Cong Truong Quoc Te (Pham Ngoc Thach / Tran Cao Van), District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A modernist 1967-1972 traffic-circle monument of five splayed concrete 'hands' and an octagonal fountain, on the site of a French water tower and an old Nguyen-era citadel gate. Now a beloved evening hangout for street snacks.

P.ad: 202 Vo Thi Sau, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A 31,000-object museum (est. 1985; Class-I museum from 2024) devoted to southern Vietnamese women in war and culture — female guerrillas, ao dai history and Mother Goddess worship. Closed Mondays; free.

P.ad: 5 Ton Duc Thang, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Riverside museum (opened 1988) to Ton Duc Thang, Vietnam's second president and a Con Dao political prisoner, with 16,000+ documents on his life and the labour movement. Closed Mondays; free.

P.ad: 104 Yersin, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The 'American Market' off Yersin St, famous since 1975 for army-surplus gear, dog tags, ponchos and militaria (genuine and replica) alongside hardware stalls — a gritty relic of the war years. Bargain and check provenance.

P.ad: 339 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia, Ward 7, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The city's largest Mahayana pagoda (built 1964-1971 with Japanese aid), the first to render traditional temple form in concrete, crowned by a seven-storey, 40 m stupa. Free.

P.ad: 89 Ba Huyen Thanh Quan, Vo Thi Sau Ward, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A seven-storey 1956-1958 pagoda that was the flashpoint of the 1963 Buddhist Crisis: the epicentre of anti-Diem protests and the 21 August 1963 army raid that arrested hundreds of monks and helped trigger the coup.

P.ad: 289 Hai Ba Trung, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The bubblegum-pink Romano-Gothic Catholic church begun 1870-1876 (its signature pink dates to a 1957 repaint) — the city's second-largest church and a landmark photo stop. Active parish; exterior always, interior around Mass times.

P.ad: 720A Dien Bien Phu, Ward 22, Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: At 461 m the tallest building in Vietnam (2018), a bamboo-cluster supertall over the Saigon River in Vinhomes Central Park. The SkyView observatory spans floors 79-81 for the city's highest panorama.

P.ad: 710 Nguyen Trai, Ward 11, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Cholon's most famous temple (Tue Thanh Guildhall), built by Cantonese immigrants around 1760 for Mazu, sea goddess of the overseas Chinese. Famed for its porcelain-figurine roof friezes and hanging incense coils. National monument.

P.ad: 57A Thap Muoi, Ward 2, District 6 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Cholon's grand wholesale market, financed by merchant Quach Dam and completed 1928, built around a pagoda-roofed courtyard; a recognised heritage building (restored 2016-2018) and still a major distribution hub.

P.ad: 25 Hoc Lac, Ward 14, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Cholon's Chinese-Catholic parish church (1900-1902), Gothic with Chinese detailing. Here President Ngo Dinh Diem and his brother took refuge and surrendered during the 1 November 1963 coup, before being killed en route.

P.ad: 678 Nguyen Trai, Ward 11, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A 19th-century Teochew guildhall temple to the deified warlord Quan Cong, one of Cholon's oldest, celebrated for its gilded woodwork, a huge red-lacquer horse of Quan Cong and intricate roof ceramics.

P.ad: 264 Hai Thuong Lan Ong, Ward 14, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A Fujianese assembly-hall temple (Nhi Phu Hoi Quan, from the late 17th/18th c.) venerating Ong Bon, guardian god of land and wealth; ship-prow roofs, carved red pillars and a national relic listing (1998).

P.ad: 802 Nguyen Trai, Ward 14, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A southern-Fujian (Zhangzhou) guildhall temple founded 1809 for Thien Hau, with four China-carved dragon-wrapped stone pillars shipped in by boat and vivid ceramic roof scenes; especially alive at the Lantern Festival.

P.ad: 565 Lac Long Quan, Ward 10, Tan Binh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Believed the oldest temple in the city (founded 1744), atmospheric in garden grounds with a Bodhi tree, a nine-tier stupa and thousands of decorative plates set into its walls. National relic. Free.

P.ad: Long Hoa, Hoa Thanh, Tay Ninh Province, Vietnam (day trip ~90 km NW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
P.w: The kaleidoscopic 1933-1955 Great Temple of Caodaism, Vietnam's homegrown syncretic religion, with a divine 'all-seeing eye', dragon pillars and rainbow interior. Time a visit for the white-robed noon ceremony. Often paired with Cu Chi.

P.n: Mekong Delta Day Trip (My Tho & Ben Tre)
P.ad: My Tho (Tien Giang) & Ben Tre Provinces, Vietnam (day trip ~70-90 km SW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
P.w: The classic close Delta day trip: a Tien River cruise past the Dragon/Unicorn/Phoenix/Tortoise islets, sampan rides through coconut-palm canals, a coconut-candy workshop, honey tea and the large Vinh Trang Pagoda at My Tho.

P.ad: Ninh Son, Tay Ninh Province, Vietnam (day trip ~100 km NW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
P.w: The 986 m 'Black Virgin Mountain', highest peak in the south, a pilgrimage site of cave temples reached by a Guinness-record cable-car system to Sun World, with a 72 m bronze Bodhisattva at the summit. Pairs with Tay Ninh's Cao Dai temple.

P.n: Can Gio Mangrove Biosphere Reserve (Monkey Island)
P.ad: Can Gio District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (~50-60 km SE of the centre)
P.w: Vietnam's first UNESCO Man-and-Biosphere reserve (designated 2000), a replanted mangrove forest that was the Viet Cong's Rung Sac guerrilla zone. Boat trips, a reconstructed guerrilla base, crocodile lagoons and a large troop of macaques ('Monkey Island').

P.ad: Cai Rang District, Can Tho, Mekong Delta, Vietnam (long day trip / overnight ~170 km SW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
P.w: The biggest floating wholesale market in the Delta, where boats trade produce hung from tall poles at dawn on the Can Tho River. Deep in the Delta (~3.5 hrs each way) — best as an early-start long day trip or overnight; trades wind down by ~08:30.

P.ad: Ha Long St, Ward 2, Vung Tau, Ba Ria-Vung Tau Province, Vietnam (day trip ~95 km / 2-hr ferry from Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
P.w: The nearest beach escape: a seaside town crowned by a 32 m Christ the King statue (1974) you can climb (~800 steps inside) for coastal views, plus the White Palace and Back Beach. Reachable by road or Saigon River fast ferry.

P.ad: Kuala Lumpur City Centre (KLCC), Jalan Ampang, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
P.w: The 452 m twin towers with the double-decker skybridge — KL's defining landmark, once the world's tallest buildings.

P.ad: Gombak, Selangor (Greater Kuala Lumpur), Malaysia
P.w: A limestone hill of Hindu cave temples reached by 272 rainbow steps under the giant golden Murugan statue; focus of the Thaipusam festival.

P.ad: George Town, Penang, Malaysia
P.w: The UNESCO-listed old town of clan jetties, shophouses, temples and the famous street-art murals (part of 'Melaka and George Town, Historic Cities of the Straits of Malacca').

P.ad: Air Itam, Penang, Malaysia
P.w: Southeast Asia's largest Chinese Buddhist temple, with the Pagoda of Ten Thousand Buddhas and a 30 m bronze Kuan Yin.

P.n: Cheong Fatt Tze — The Blue Mansion
P.ad: 14 Leith Street, George Town, Penang, Malaysia
P.w: The indigo-blue Hakka merchant mansion, a multi-award-winning heritage restoration and film location ('Crazy Rich Asians').

P.ad: Bandar Hilir, Malacca (Melaka), Malaysia
P.w: The 1511 Portuguese fort gate (Porta de Santiago), the red Dutch Stadthuys/Christ Church and Jonker Street — the heart of UNESCO Malacca.

P.ad: Na Phra Lan Road, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand
P.w: The 1782 royal palace complex and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha — Thailand's most sacred and most-visited site.

P.ad: 158 Thanon Wang Doem, Bangkok Yai, Bangkok, Thailand
P.w: The Temple of Dawn, its porcelain-encrusted riverside prang rising over the Chao Phraya.

P.ad: 2 Sanam Chai Road, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand
P.w: Home of the 46 m gold-leafed Reclining Buddha and the birthplace of traditional Thai massage.

P.ad: 587/10 Kamphaeng Phet 2 Road, Chatuchak, Bangkok, Thailand
P.w: One of the world's largest weekend markets — 15,000+ stalls of food, crafts, plants and vintage.

P.ad: Doi Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, Thailand
P.w: The gold-chedi mountain temple above Chiang Mai, reached by a 300-step naga staircase — the city's emblem.

P.n: Chiang Mai Old City Temples (Wat Chedi Luang & Wat Phra Singh)
P.ad: Old City (within the moat), Chiang Mai, Thailand
P.w: The walled Old City's Lanna temples — the ruined 14th-century Chedi Luang and the revered Wat Phra Singh.

P.ad: 28 Vo Van Tan Street, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: HCMC's unflinching museum of the Indochina and Vietnam wars — the city's most affecting historical site.

P.ad: Le Loi, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The landmark 1914 central market — street food, textiles and souvenirs in the heart of Saigon.

P.ad: Cu Chi District (Ben Dinh / Ben Duoc), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The vast wartime underground tunnel network northwest of the city — a defining day trip from Saigon.

P.n: Hoan Kiem Lake, Ngoc Son Temple & the Old Quarter
P.ad: Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
P.w: Hanoi's civic heart — the legendary lake and its red bridge to Ngoc Son Temple, ringed by the 36-streets Old Quarter.

P.ad: Quang Ninh Province (day trip / cruise from Hanoi), Vietnam
P.w: The UNESCO seascape of thousands of limestone karst islands — Vietnam's iconic natural wonder.

P.ad: Hoi An, Quang Nam Province, Vietnam
P.w: The UNESCO-listed trading port of lantern-lit streets, Japanese Covered Bridge and preserved merchant houses.

P.ad: Magelang Regency (near Yogyakarta), Central Java, Indonesia
P.w: The world's largest Buddhist temple, a 9th-century stupa-mountain of 2,600+ relief panels — UNESCO World Heritage.

P.ad: Sleman (Yogyakarta–Central Java border), Indonesia
P.w: Indonesia's largest Hindu temple compound, a soaring 9th-century Shiva complex — UNESCO World Heritage.

P.ad: Pecatu, South Kuta, Bali, Indonesia
P.w: A sea temple perched on a 70 m cliff above the Indian Ocean, famous for sunset and the kecak fire dance.

P.ad: Beraban, Kediri, Tabanan, Bali, Indonesia
P.w: The much-photographed sea temple on a tidal rock offshore — Bali's classic sunset silhouette.

P.ad: Tegallalang, north of Ubud, Bali, Indonesia
P.w: The emerald stepped paddies of the subak system — part of Bali's only UNESCO site, the Cultural Landscape of Bali Province.

P.ad: West Jakarta, Jakarta, Indonesia
P.w: The Dutch-colonial old town around Fatahillah Square, with the Jakarta History Museum and Cafe Batavia.

P.ad: Intramuros, Manila, Philippines
P.w: The 16th-century Spanish walled city — cobbled streets, bastions and Fort Santiago, the historic core of Manila.

P.ad: General Luna Street, Intramuros, Manila, Philippines
P.w: The oldest stone church in the Philippines (1607) and a UNESCO 'Baroque Churches of the Philippines' World Heritage site.

P.ad: Ermita, Manila, Philippines
P.w: The historic seaside park at the site of national hero Jose Rizal's execution, marked by the Rizal Monument.

P.n: Basilica Minore del Santo Nino & Magellan's Cross
P.ad: Osmena Boulevard / P. Burgos Street, Cebu City, Philippines
P.w: The country's oldest Catholic relic and church, beside the 1521 cross planted at Magellan's arrival — the cradle of Philippine Christianity.

P.ad: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap, Cambodia
P.w: The largest religious monument on earth, the 12th-century Khmer temple-city and Cambodia's national symbol — UNESCO World Heritage.

P.ad: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap, Cambodia
P.w: The walled royal city of Angkor Thom and the Bayon's forest of giant serene stone faces.

P.ad: Sothearos Boulevard, Phnom Penh, Cambodia
P.w: The Khmer royal palace complex on the riverfront, including the Silver Pagoda with its emerald and gold Buddhas.

P.n: Luang Prabang Old Town (Wat Xieng Thong)
P.ad: Luang Prabang peninsula, Laos
P.w: The UNESCO-listed royal town where Lao and French-colonial architecture meet, crowned by the 1560 Wat Xieng Thong and the dawn alms-giving.

P.ad: ~29 km south of Luang Prabang, Laos
P.w: Turquoise multi-tiered travertine waterfalls in the jungle — Luang Prabang's signature natural excursion.

P.ad: Singuttara Hill, Yangon, Myanmar
P.w: Myanmar's most sacred Buddhist site — a 112 m gold-plated stupa said to enshrine relics of the Buddha.

P.ad: Bagan, Mandalay Region, Myanmar
P.w: A plain studded with thousands of 11th–13th-century Buddhist temples and pagodas — UNESCO World Heritage.

P.ad: 18 Marina Gardens Drive, Marina Bay
P.w: Waterfront nature park with the Supertree Grove, Cloud Forest & Flower Dome; over 1.5 million plants.

P.n: Marina Bay Sands SkyPark Observation Deck
P.ad: 10 Bayfront Avenue, Marina Bay
P.w: The 57th-storey deck atop Marina Bay Sands' three towers, with panoramic skyline views over the bay.

P.ad: 1 Fullerton Road, Marina Bay
P.w: Home of the 8.6 m Merlion, Singapore's lion-headed, fish-bodied national symbol, spouting into the bay.

P.ad: 6 Bayfront Avenue, Marina Bay
P.w: Lotus-shaped museum at Marina Bay Sands; home to the teamLab 'Future World' digital art gallery.

P.ad: 30 Raffles Avenue, Marina Bay
P.w: A 165 m observation wheel over Marina Bay with views to the city, the Straits and beyond.

P.ad: 1 St Andrew's Road, Civic District
P.w: World's largest public collection of Singapore & Southeast Asian art, in the former City Hall & Supreme Court.

P.ad: 93 Stamford Road, Civic District
P.w: The nation's oldest museum (est. 1849), narrating Singapore's social history.

P.ad: 1 Empress Place, Civic District
P.w: Riverside museum devoted to the material cultures of Asia, from Chinese to West Asian civilisations.

P.ad: 1 Beach Road, Civic District
P.w: 1887 colonial-era grande dame; a National Monument and birthplace of the Singapore Sling.

P.ad: River Valley Road, Fort Canning
P.w: Historic hilltop park with artefacts dating to the 1300s; the famous Fort Canning tree tunnel.

P.ad: 1 Esplanade Drive, Marina Bay
P.w: The 'durian' performing-arts centre on the bayfront, a defining piece of the skyline.

P.ad: 244 South Bridge Road, Chinatown
P.w: Singapore's oldest Hindu temple (1827); a National Monument with a vivid gopuram tower.

P.ad: 288 South Bridge Road, Chinatown
P.w: Tang-style Buddhist temple (2007) housing a sacred tooth relic in a 3,500 kg gold stupa.

P.ad: 158 Telok Ayer Street, Chinatown
P.w: Singapore's oldest Hokkien temple (1839) dedicated to Mazu; a National Monument built without nails.

P.ad: 48 Pagoda Street, Chinatown
P.w: Recreated 1950s shophouse interiors telling the story of Chinatown's early immigrant tenants.

P.ad: 3 Muscat Street, Kampong Glam
P.w: Kampong Glam's golden-domed royal mosque; a National Monument and the heart of the Malay-Arab quarter.

P.ad: 141 Serangoon Road, Little India
P.w: Little India's landmark Hindu temple to the goddess Kali, founded by Tamil lime-kiln workers (1855).

P.n: Former House of Tan Teng Niah
P.ad: 37 Kerbau Road, Little India
P.w: The last surviving Chinese villa in Little India (1900), painted in vivid rainbow colours.

P.n: Koon Seng Road Peranakan Shophouses (Joo Chiat/Katong)
P.ad: Koon Seng Road, Joo Chiat
P.w: Singapore's most photographed row of pastel Peranakan shophouses (1920s) in the Katong-Joo Chiat conservation area.

P.n: Jewel Changi Airport & HSBC Rain Vortex
P.ad: 78 Airport Boulevard, Changi Airport
P.w: Glass-domed nature-and-retail complex housing the world's tallest indoor waterfall (40 m) and Shiseido Forest Valley.

P.ad: 1000 Upper Changi Road North, Changi
P.w: NHB museum commemorating WWII POWs interned at Changi, with a replica of the Changi Chapel.

P.ad: East Coast Park Service Road, Marine Parade
P.w: Singapore's largest seaside park; 15 km of coastline for cycling, seafood and the sea breeze.

P.ad: 1 Geylang Serai
P.w: The cultural heart of the Malay-Muslim community; a bustling wet market and Ramadan bazaar hub.

P.ad: 1 Cluny Road, Bukit Timah
P.w: Singapore's first UNESCO World Heritage Site (2015); a 160-year-old tropical garden with the National Orchid Garden.

P.ad: Henderson Road, Mount Faber / Telok Blangah
P.w: 10 km of ridge-top trails linking Mount Faber, Telok Blangah & Kent Ridge, crossing the wave-form Henderson Waves, Singapore's highest pedestrian bridge.

P.ad: 262 Pasir Panjang Road
P.w: 1937 cultural theme park (ex-Tiger Balm Garden) of surreal dioramas, famed for the Ten Courts of Hell.

P.ad: MacRitchie Reservoir Park, Lornie Road
P.w: Central Catchment rainforest reservoir with a 250 m suspension bridge, 25 m up in the forest canopy.

P.ad: 177 Hindhede Drive, Bukit Timah
P.w: ASEAN Heritage Park protecting primary rainforest and Singapore's highest natural point (163 m).

P.ad: 80 Mandai Lake Road, Mandai
P.w: World-renowned open-concept zoo of over 4,200 animals in naturalistic, cage-free habitats.

P.ad: 80 Mandai Lake Road, Mandai
P.w: The world's first nocturnal zoo (1994); tram rides through 35 hectares of after-dark habitats.

P.ad: 80 Mandai Lake Road, Mandai
P.w: Asia's only river-themed wildlife park, home to giant pandas and a giant Amazon river tank.

P.ad: Lorong Mambong, Holland Village
P.w: A long-time bohemian expat enclave of eateries, bars and shophouses off Holland Road.

P.ad: Lorong 6 Toa Payoh (in front of Blk 28), Singapore
P.w: Singapore's most iconic surviving 1979 mosaic 'dragon' playground, designed by HDB's Khor Ean Ghee — a terrazzo-tiled dragon head with a climbable ring body. One of only two dragon playgrounds left and a marquee stop on NHB's Toa Payoh Heritage Trail.

P.ad: 184 Jalan Toa Payoh, Singapore 319944
P.w: Singapore's oldest Buddhist monastery — completed 1909 and gazetted a National Monument in 1980 — modelled on Fuzhou's Xi Chan Monastery, with the Hall of Celestial Kings and Mahavira Hall laid out in the classic cong lin ('layered forest') plan.

P.n: Toa Payoh Town Park & Look-Out Tower
P.ad: Lorong 6 Toa Payoh (beside Toa Payoh HDB Hub), Singapore
P.w: The 4.8-hectare 1970s town park that pioneered greenery in HDB new towns — landscaped ponds, rustic gazebos and the conserved 25 m space-age Look-Out Tower, a favourite 1970s-80s wedding-photo backdrop.
P.k: Open daily, free; tower not accessible

P.ad: 91 Toa Payoh Central, Singapore 319193
P.w: Toa Payoh's first Catholic church (inaugurated 1971), a modernist landmark at the junction of Toa Payoh Central and Lorong 4 that has long offered Mass in English, Mandarin and Tamil — featured on the Toa Payoh Heritage Trail's 'Of Faiths & Beliefs' route.

P.ad: 53 Lorong 5 Toa Payoh, Singapore 310053
P.w: The Y-shaped 1967 HDB showpiece with a rooftop viewing gallery once used to survey the young new town from above. Queen Elizabeth II visited in 1972 (as did Princess Anne, Prince Philip and other dignitaries), earning it the 'VIP Block' name.
P.k: Rooftop gallery closed; view from ground level

P.ad: 480 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, Singapore 310480
P.w: HDB's headquarters and the civic heart of Singapore's first fully HDB-built satellite town, home to relocated public sculptures — Ng Eng Teng's 'The Climb', Chong Fah Cheong's 'Mama's Precious One' and Ju Ming's 'Tai Chi Boxing' — plus a mall, library and hawker fare.

P.ad: Toa Payoh Central (trail starts near HDB Hub), Singapore
P.w: NHB's self-guided trail through Singapore's second satellite town, linking 16-plus sites — from the Dragon Playground and Town Park to Shuang Lin Monastery — across two themed routes, 'Of Public Housing & Shared Spaces' and 'Of Faiths & Beliefs'.

P.n: United Temple (United Five Temples of Toa Payoh)
P.ad: Lorong 6 Toa Payoh (near Blk 177/178), Singapore
P.w: Established 1974, the first temple in Singapore to house smaller constituent temples under one roof — five village temples (Chee Tian Keng, Shan Zu Yuan Fu De Ci, Tong Xing Gang, Zhao Ying Ci and others) that were displaced when Toa Payoh's kampongs were cleared pooled their devotees' funds to build here. A landmark on NHB's Toa Payoh Heritage Trail 'Of Faiths & Beliefs' route.

P.ad: 2001 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, Singapore 319259
P.w: A Dravidian-style Hindu temple to the goddess Kaliamman, tracing to an 1860 shrine near Orchard Road and rebuilt at Toa Payoh in 1982 (consecrated 1986). Notable for founding Saraswathi Kindergarten, said to be Singapore's first pre-school, and a stop on the Toa Payoh Heritage Trail's 'Of Faiths & Beliefs' route.

P.ad: Lorong 5 / Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, Singapore
P.w: Singapore's first sensory park (opened 2009), a 1.1-hectare garden by Surbana and Yoshisuke Miyake split into five zones for sight, smell, touch, sound and taste — with larger-than-life optical-illusion mirrors that reveal a hidden face, resonating steel 'drum' plates, a playground and a fragrant garden.

P.ad: 6 Toa Payoh Central, Singapore 319191
P.w: Inaugurated 7 Feb 1974, the second public library of the 1970s branch-building drive and a civic anchor of the town — its Children's Section riffs on the iconic dragon playground with hexagonal mosaic-tile motifs. A pioneering heartland library documented in NLB's BiblioAsia.
P.k: Free; closed Mondays historically — check hours

P.n: Toa Payoh Seu Teck Sean Tong
P.ad: 15 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh (Kampong Hup Choon Hng site), Singapore
P.w: A Chinese charitable temple established as an attap hut in 1942 and rebuilt 1959, enshrining the deity Song Da Feng and blending Buddhist, Taoist and Confucian rites. Its medical wing (opened 1967) still gives free Traditional Chinese Medicine consultations — a living community institution on the heritage trail.

P.ad: Toa Payoh MRT Station (NS19), 480 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, Singapore

F.w: Serving one dish since 1960; drier prawn-stock Hokkien mee with a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.ad: #01-41 Bedok South Market & Food Centre, 16 Bedok South Road
F.w: Since 1961; full-bodied wok-hei char kway teow with cockles, a Michelin Bib and 40-min queues.

F.n: Lao Fu Zi Fried Kway Teow
F.ad: #01-12 Old Airport Road Food Centre, 51 Old Airport Road
F.w: Smoky wok-hei CKT with blood cockles & lup cheong; a 2025 Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.ad: #01-135/136 Old Airport Road Food Centre, 51 Old Airport Road
F.w: Teochew kway chap since the 1980s; immaculately cleaned braised offal, a 2025 Michelin Bib.

F.ad: #01-121 Old Airport Road Food Centre, 51 Old Airport Road
F.w: KL-style caramelised char siew on pork belly; a modern hawker favourite.

F.ad: 204 East Coast Road, Katong/Joo Chiat
F.w: 101-year-old Hainanese kopitiam; iconic round charcoal kaya buns, reopened 2021.

F.ad: 38/40 Joo Chiat Place, Joo Chiat
F.w: Singapore's oldest Peranakan restaurant (1953); traditional Nonya cooking, third generation.

F.n: Mr & Mrs Mohgan's Super Crispy Roti Prata
F.ad: 300 Joo Chiat Road (Tin Yeang Coffeeshop)
F.w: Cult super-crispy prata cooked to order; long morning queues, 'cult status entirely affirmed'.

F.ad: 237 Geylang Road (Geylang Lorong 9)
F.w: Iconic Geylang beef hor fun with goopy black bean gravy; in the 2025 Michelin Guide.

F.ad: #01-05 East Coast Lagoon Food Village, 1220 East Coast Parkway
F.w: East Coast Lagoon's beloved Malay-Muslim satay, grilled seaside over charcoal.

F.n: Kway Guan Huat Joo Chiat Popiah
F.ad: 95 Joo Chiat Road, Joo Chiat
F.w: Since 1938; hand-made popiah skins spun on a wooden pole, a Joo Chiat heritage name.

F.n: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
F.ad: #01-01, 439 Joo Chiat Road, Joo Chiat
F.w: 40-year-old claypot bak kut teh with pepper & garlic; a 2025 Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.ad: 247 Joo Chiat Place, Joo Chiat (original; premises sold Aug 2025)
F.w: The legendary Joo Chiat/Still Road black pepper crab; original shophouse closed Aug 2025 after the premises sold (crew relocated to a Tampines industrial canteen).

F.ad: #01-15 Adam Road Food Centre, 2 Adam Road, Bukit Timah
F.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand nasi lemak on basmati; reportedly a favourite of the Sultan of Brunei.

F.ad: 1 Thong Soon Avenue, Upper Thomson
F.w: Famous Upper Thomson prata with 60+ flavours from the Murtaburger to Prata Alfredo.

F.ad: Block 17A Dempsey Road, Dempsey Hill
F.w: The world's first Michelin-starred Peranakan restaurant; Chef Malcolm Lee's elevated Straits-Chinese cooking.

F.ad: 7 Dempsey Road, Dempsey Hill
F.w: One Michelin star & Asia's 50 Best; wood-fired modern barbecue, near-impossible reservations.

F.ad: 399/401/403 Balestier Road
F.w: A chicken rice institution since 1979; promoted to Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2025.

F.ad: 347 Balestier Road
F.w: Peppery Teochew bak kut teh open late for supper; a Balestier landmark.

F.n: Margaret Drive Sin Kee Chicken Rice
F.ad: #02-06 Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, 44 Holland Drive
F.w: Steamed chicken rice since 1978; on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list since 2018.

F.n: Depot Road Zhen Shan Mei Claypot Laksa
F.ad: #01-75 Alexandra Village Food Centre, 120 Bukit Merah Lane 1
F.w: Multi-time award-winning laksa (Michelin Bib 2016+) rich with cockles and prawns.

F.ad: #02-185 Bukit Timah Market & Food Centre, 51 Upper Bukit Timah Road
F.w: Famous white chai tow kway near Beauty World; crisp, wok-fried and eggy.

F.ad: #01-49 Redhill Food Centre, 85 Redhill Lane
F.w: 'Mickey Mouse' chai tow kway, radish cake made from scratch daily; Michelin Bib since 2019.

F.ad: #01-06 Commonwealth Crescent Market & Food Centre, 31 Commonwealth Crescent
F.w: Charcoal-roasted char siew with an ideal fat-to-meat ratio; reopened after a two-year hiatus.

F.ad: #01-120 ABC Brickworks Market & Food Centre, 6 Jalan Bukit Merah
F.w: 34 years of sweet, succulent char siew and roast meats at ABC Brickworks.

F.ad: #01-40 Yuhua Village Market & Food Centre, 254 Jurong East Street 24
F.w: Charcoal-roasted meats & wanton mee in Jurong East; Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.ad: Block 505 Jurong West Street 52 (Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre)
F.w: Nostalgic old-school wanton mee in Jurong West; new to the 2025 Michelin Guide.

F.ad: #01-06 Boon Lay Place Food Village, 221B Boon Lay Place
F.w: A big-name Jurong nasi lemak using extra-virgin coconut oil.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-30, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2016 — two sisters fry each plate of crispy-yet-spongy white carrot cake to order, drawing long queues at the freshly renovated (reopened Aug 2025) Toa Payoh West hawker centre.

F.n: Come Daily Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee
F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-27, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: Michelin-listed and running since 1968, Steven Ng reduces prawn stock right in the wok for one of Toa Payoh's most famous plates of Hokkien mee — a fixture of the reopened Toa Payoh West food centre.

F.n: Hai Nan Xing Zhou Beef Noodle
F.ad: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-06, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
F.w: Nearly 70 years of Hainanese beef noodles from S$5, newly awarded a Michelin Bib Gourmand — dry or soup, in a rich braise the whole hawker centre queues for.

F.ad: Block A, Jackson Square, 11 Toa Payoh Lorong 3, S319579
F.w: A Michelin-starred Cantonese chef sells $5 wanton mee from a warehouse-canteen stall — HK-shipped springy noodles and charred char siew that earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand within a year of opening (still listed 2025/2026).

F.ad: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-20, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
F.w: The original stall of Singapore's 58-year-old fishball dynasty (est. 1968), Michelin Bib Gourmand for four years running since 2022 — springy, umami yellowtail fishballs made fresh daily.

F.ad: Blk 20 Toa Payoh Lorong 7 coffeeshop, S310020
F.w: A beloved $1 nasi lemak that has held its price since 1987 to stay affordable for elderly regulars — cooking starts at 4am and 300-500 plates sell out by midday; covered by every major food outlet and YouTuber Ghib Ojisan.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 5 Food Centre, #01-31, Blk 75 Lorong 5 Toa Payoh, S310075
F.w: A cult chicken rice stall that swaps roast/poached chicken for addictively marinated crispy fried wings ($3.50) with a spicy chilli dip — famously long evening queues until sold out.

F.ad: Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, #01-58, S310022
F.w: The Toa Payoh outlet of Uncle David Ng's famed noodle stall, where bouncy yellowtail fishballs are hand-pounded on the spot (the Holland Drive original holds the Michelin Bib Gourmand).

F.ad: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-03, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
F.w: A 3rd-generation popiah stall with roots to 1930, hand-rolling Hokkien-style popiah (no pork, no lard, no MSG) with house-fried sole-fish crisps — one of Singapore's most heritage popiah names.

F.n: Lai Heng Mushroom Minced Meat Noodle
F.ad: Blk 73 Toa Payoh Lorong 5, Toa Payoh
F.w: A bak chor mee institution running since 1985 (relocated twice within Toa Payoh), still turning out a spicy dry mee kia and a standout lard-rich kway teow soup that Seth Lui rated after 24 years of visits.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-34, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: UK-trained ex-engineer Anton Tan turned his family's zi char stall into a viral $1.20 muffin institution — deliberately misshapen buns with crunchy caramelised crusts; a long-queue hawker-dessert cult reopened after the 2025 renovation.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: A 30-plus-year heritage pau stall (est. 1993, three years on the Michelin Plate) hand-making Teochew-style buns with thick, not-too-sweet lotus paste — announced closure end-2025 but reopened June 2026 after public demand.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: Two sisters plate one of Singapore's most generous $5 thunder tea rice sets — less oil, less salt, no MSG — with the fragrant bitter-green tea broth poured over brown rice and crunchy toppings.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: Ex-Italian-restaurant cook Desheng makes beancurd from scratch daily with non-GMO soybeans — smooth, un-gritty tau huay you can dress with gula melaka, grass jelly or gingko.

F.n: Toa Payoh Scissors Cut Curry Rice
F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
F.w: Old-school Hainanese-style curry rice from S$2.80 — a heaped plate of chopped sides flooded in three different gravies (curry, braise, pork), a comfort-food fixture of Lorong 8.

F.n: Uncle Kun's Delicacies (Kun Shu Food Stall)
F.ad: Toa Payoh Vista Market, Lorong 4 Toa Payoh
F.w: Ex-hotel HK chef Lam Kun serves restaurant-grade dim sum at hawker prices; his signature oblong scallop glutinous rice (S$4.80), packed with dried scallop, salted egg and lap cheong, isn't found elsewhere in Singapore.

F.n: Min Kee Tanjong Rhu Wanton Noodle
F.ad: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
F.w: A decades-old wanton mee that relocated from Tanjong Rhu, still selling a substantial $3.50 bowl of springy noodles with black-chilli option, soupy and fried wantons — a Kim Keat breakfast favourite.

F.ad: Gourmet Paradise Food Court, Toa Payoh HDB Hub, Blk 480 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, #B1-01, S310480
F.w: Likely the last hawker hand-making this Teochew snack from scratch — Teo Yong Joo mills flour, roasts peanuts and pinches each soft, tender muah chee ball to order at the HDB Hub food court.

F.ad: Blk 92 Toa Payoh Lorong 4, #01-264, S310092
F.w: Once rated among Singapore's top-five Hokkien mee — served in a heat-retaining claypot with deep-fried crispy pork belly — this 10-year Toa Payoh favourite shuttered on 28 Feb 2026. Kept here as a flagged closure.

F.n: Hup Chong Hakka Yong Tau Foo — CLOSED
F.ad: Blk 203 Toa Payoh (final location; earlier Blk 116/124)
F.w: A four-generation Hakka yong tau foo with roots to a 1952 pushcart, famous for handmade fried meatballs and fish paste — it closed for good on 28 Jan 2026 after 70-plus years amid falling footfall. Kept here as a flagged closure.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-22, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: A father-and-son team from Shenzhen mill their own rice flour on a stone grinder to make thicker, rustic cheung fun to order, tinted naturally with spinach and pink dragonfruit across 13 fillings — a standout of the reopened (Aug 2025) Toa Payoh West hawker centre.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-24, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: A no-frills stall doing a $3 bowl of fried fish ban mian — crispy fried fish slices, handmade noodles and a clean savoury broth — one of the value picks flagged across guides to the renovated Toa Payoh West food centre.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: A 20-year veteran hand-tearing mee hoon kueh dough to order and ladling fish soup and porridge — old-school comfort noodles that regulars queue for at Toa Payoh West.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, #01-79, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
F.w: The Toa Payoh outlet of the Tekka Centre briyani institution — a Michelin Plate / Michelin-recommended name whose fragrant $6 chicken, mutton and fish briyani draw a queue; the pull-apart rice and house sambal are the draw.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, #01-24, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
F.w: A 40-year Toa Payoh institution famous for selling out fast — owner Mr Ng meticulously cleans the offal for an odourless, tender braise served over silky rice sheets in a light herbal broth; widely rated among Singapore's best kway chap.

F.ad: 211 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, #01-01, S310211
F.w: An ex-hotel chef plates restaurant-grade Japanese food from a kopitiam beside the Lorong 8 hawker centre — the Tataki Salmon Roll ($6) and Butter Yaki Seabass Bento ($6.80) look far pricier than they cost; nothing on the menu tops $10.

F.n: Da Lao Fried White Kway Teow
F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, #01-23, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
F.w: A one-man wok turning out Penang-style fried white kway teow with serious wok hei — clean, coated-not-greasy strands with fish cake, lap cheong and cockles from $4; the single-hand pace means a wait, and a long queue.

F.n: Seletar Sheng Mian Mee Hoon Kway
F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
F.w: Relocated from the demolished Seletar market, this snaking-queue stall hand-kneads, smacks and tears each piece of dough for uniquely textured sheng mian in a comforting pork-and-ikan-bilis broth from $3.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, #01-07, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
F.w: Widely dubbed the best cendol in Singapore — and a favourite of ESM Goh Chok Tong, whose photos line the stall — with firmly-packed ice that stays solid, springy pandan jelly and gula melaka, plus Mao Shan Wang / D24 durian tops.

F.n: Song Kee Kway Teow Noodle Soup
F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 5 Food Centre, Blk 75 Lorong 5 Toa Payoh, S310075
F.w: A 16-year evening-only stall (5pm–midnight) whose fishballs are pounded from scratch at 3am — bouncy, fresh yellowtail fishballs and fragrant fish dumplings over springy mee pok that fans call the best in Singapore.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 5 Food Centre, #01-25, Blk 75 Lorong 5 Toa Payoh, S310075
F.w: A 1966 satay stall now in its third generation, grilling well-marinated Chinese-style chicken and pork skewers over charcoal to order — beautifully charred sticks served with peanut sauce and fresh pineapple gravy.

F.ad: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-25, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
F.w: A 50-year-old orh chien specialist (open ~3 hours a day) frying crisp-yet-chewy potato-starch batter with fluffy egg and juicy large Korean oysters, finished with crunchy parsley — a repeat pick on 'best oyster omelette' lists.

F.ad: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
F.w: The stall with Kim Keat Palm's longest breakfast queue — wok-fried bee hoon and noodles with cabbage, best paired with a runny-yolk sunny-side-up egg; a heartland morning staple.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Palm Spring Market, Blk 93 Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, S310093
F.w: A second-generation kway chap running since 1967 and rated Singapore's best-rated kway chap — spice-forward braised innards, tau pok and silky rice sheets from 5.30pm, with snaking queues before it even opens.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Palm Spring Market, Blk 93 Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, S310093
F.w: A 58-year cult favourite with arguably the longest queue in Palm Spring from 6am — springy mee pok tossed in a punchy chilli sauce with hand-made fishballs and meatballs; dry or soup.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Vista Market, 74 Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, S310074
F.w: A Vista Market morning fixture drawing daily queues for crisp roti prata — plain to cheese-and-egg and sweet banana — then Indian-Muslim mee goreng, nasi goreng merah and tulang merah after 1.30pm; carries a Makansutra 'Divine' rating.

F.ad: Gourmet Paradise Food Court, Toa Payoh HDB Hub, #B1-01, Blk 480 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, S310480
F.w: A decades-old rojak stall by the HDB Hub food-court escalator with a permanent 20-30 minute queue — a generous mountain of youtiao, cucumber, pineapple, turnip and cuttlefish drowned in prawn-paste, torch-ginger and mounds of peanut.

F.n: Biang Biang Noodles Xi'an Famous Food
F.ad: Food Alley, 190 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, #01-518, Toa Payoh Central, S310190
F.w: A rare hawker source of Xi'an biang biang noodles — extra-wide belt noodles hand-stretched and slapped against the counter, tossed with braised pork, tomato-egg and chilli, plus rou jia mo (Chinese 'burger'); a hidden gem at Toa Payoh Central's Food Alley.

F.ad: Blk 73 Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, #01-585, S310073
F.w: A young-hawker zi char revival — five friends in their late twenties reopened a founder's father's stall, cooking almost a hundred dishes rich in wok hei at hawker prices, from sambal kang kong to inventive Imperial Cereal Milk Pork.

F.ad: Blk 125 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, #01-, S310125
F.w: A husband-and-wife stall (she's Vietnamese) doing soul-comforting pho with broth simmered 8 hours on beef shank and shin, plus crisp fried spring rolls stuffed with pork, prawn and glass noodles — sauces imported from Vietnam, everything under $10.

F.ad: Blk 128 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, #01-829, S310128
F.w: The original heartland home of a beloved SG ice-cream name — handcrafted scoops like Earl Grey Lavender and Sea Salt Gula Melaka over freshly-pressed, crisp-outside pillowy Belgian waffles; the Toa Payoh dessert stop.

F.ad: Blk 128 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, #01-833, S310128
F.w: An under-rated heartland cafe run by a France-trained baker — everything is handmade in-house, from crusty tiger bread and light not-too-sweet cakes to a Nyonya chendol waffle; a quaint wooden-front hideout beside Creamier.

F.ad: Blk 85C Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, #01-385, S310085
F.w: A hole-in-the-wall HDB cake cafe by three pastry-chef friends selling atas bakes from $3.50 — the chio Watermelon Rose cake (a nod to Black Star Pastry) and fudgy brownies among biscotti, pound cakes and cookies.
